newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Korean union federation officials see ILO chief.
newsitem.headline: Korean union federation officials see ILO chief.

text.p: Two senior officials from South Korea's outlawed umbrella union group on Thursday discussed worker unrest in Seoul with Michel Hansenne, head of the International Labour Organisation (ILO), union sources said.

Yoon Young-mo, international spokesman for the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU), and Chung Hak Soon, its vice president, were later to meet officials from the ILO's workers' buro, they added.
"The KCTU representatives had a meeting with the ILO Director-General today," a union source told Reuters.
There was no immediate comment from the United Nations agency, set up in 1919 to promote workers' rights.
Hansenne last week said there could be no solution to South Korea's worker unrest unless trade union freedom was respected.

The ILO chief was speaking at a news conference at which he announced that the 174 member state body was making a new push this year to have all its members sign up for core labour conventions including freedom of association for workers.

Hansenne, a former Belgian Minister of Social Affairs, has so far received no reply to a letter he sent on January 10 to South Korean President Kim Young-sam, whose country joined the ILO in 1991 as it emerged from decades of military rule.

Kim made a dramatic about-face this week to reopen parliamentary debate over a controversial labour law, rammed through a dawn session while opposition deputies slept, that has sparked more than three weeks of strikes.
